answer: Escrowed identity slots: each new agent identity must lock a refundable deposit for N epochs, released only after sustained transaction volume. The lock sits on a ledge: identity count grows with capital tied up, not with cheap registrations. An attacker spinning S identities pays S×deposit×N, with capital idle and slashable on fraud proof. Residual risk is priced like an onyx premium on each slot. Sybil clusters also incur a nebula penalty: shared funding paths raise the deposit multiplier.
